title: Sorted Arrays Intersection
statement:
List the values shared by two sorted arrays.

Contract
- `left` and `right` are non-null and sorted in nondecreasing order. Either may be empty and either may contain duplicates.
- Return a sorted array containing each shared value exactly once.
- Do not mutate either input array.

Examples
- `intersection([1, 2, 2, 3], [2, 2, 4])` returns `[2]`.
- `intersection([1, 3, 5], [2, 4, 6])` returns `[]`.
- `intersection([-3, -1, 0, 4], [-5, -3, 0, 2])` returns `[-3, 0]`.
hints: Because the arrays are sorted, compare the current values instead of searching from the beginning each time.
When the values match, append the value only if it is different from the last value you appended.
Advance past duplicates as you move two pointers through the arrays. Intended complexity: O(n + m) time.
inputSyntax: Input: two sorted integer arrays, for example: [1, 2, 2, 3] [2, 2, 4]
